clue.text: Human bones found in circles

definitions.meaning: the forearm has two long bones, each called a radius, and this is their plural
every circle has lines running from its centre to its edge, and this is their plural name

explanation.surface: An archaeologist turns up skeletal remains laid out in stone rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one plural: the forearm bones, and the centre-to-rim lines of geometry.

clue.text: Rubbishy figure played repeatedly by a flash person

parts.note: a riff is a short musical phrase repeated over and over in jazz or rock
a raff, in Chambers, is a worthless fellow; the same root gives raffish, meaning flashy and vulgar

explanation.surface: A guitarist's cheap hook, played on a loop by some show-off, is dismissed as trash.
explanation.walkthrough: RAFF is a rare Chambers word for a low, worthless sort; 'flash' here is the British sense of showy and vulgar, as in raffish.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff can be used as an adjective for worthless, low-grade people or things, so it stands for trashy.

clue.text: Rude man fabricated wood

indicators.note: something fabricated is made up or put together, so these letters are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: An impolite carpenter has knocked something together out of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Duramen is the botanist's term for heartwood, the dense dead core of a tree trunk.

clue.text: I governed this country

parts.note: to run a country is to govern it, so the past tense gives ran

explanation.surface: A ruler boasts of having once held power over a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation, once called Persia, which a former shah could truthfully say he ruled.

clue.text: Worker hesitating to join political party

parts.note: Labour is one of the two main British political parties
er is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: An undecided employee is thinking about signing up with a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual hand doing physical toil, such as a builder's mate, is a kind of worker.

clue.text: With abandon I, Tony, felt a face lovingly

indicators.note: doing something with abandon means wildly and without restraint, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone recounts recklessly stroking another person's cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with warm fondness and tenderness is doing it lovingly.

clue.text: Al began to chop half the stone

indicators.note: only half of the word chop is used, its last two letters

explanation.surface: A man named Al set about splitting a rock in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'began to' is a link here, though it reads as part of the story; the second half of 'chop' comes first and then Al's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, prized for its play of colour.

clue.text: Social gathering after second marriage, possibly

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, a second time
a marriage is a union between two people

explanation.surface: A party is thrown after someone weds for the second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' admits the playful reading: a second union is a re-union.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-together of old classmates or family members is a reunion.

clue.text: Steward again joined the first lady

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
in Genesis Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: An estate manager has once more teamed up with the President's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval English official who managed a manor or district on behalf of its lord.

clue.text: Without one, cmos cops error, I imagine

definitions.text: Without one, cmos cops error, I imagine

indicators.note: to imagine is to make something up in the mind, so these letters are freely reworked

explanation.surface: A tech commentator supposes that without a chip at its heart, a CMOS circuit falls into error.
explanation.walkthrough: CMOS is a kind of chip technology; the whole clue doubles as a comment that a CMOS system goes wrong without the central chip.
explanation.definitionFit: The central processing chip of a computer is what a CMOS circuit would be lost without.

clue.text: Farrier reshod the racing team

indicators.note: a horse that is reshod has its shoes refitted, so these letters are refitted too

explanation.surface: A blacksmith puts new shoes on the horses of a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrari is the Italian Formula One team, famous for its red cars.

clue.text: To present, chin, prominently

definitions.meaning: to give a starring place to something, as a magazine or film does
the chin is one part of the face, as are the nose and eyes

explanation.surface: A host introduces someone whose jaw juts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prominently' extends the first sense: to present something prominently is to give it top billing.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for giving something star billing, and a noun for any part of the face such as the jaw.

clue.text: Rob an artist and politician

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A thief targets a painter and a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramp is an old British slang verb meaning to swindle or extort money from someone.

clue.text: Course food that's about right

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, as something about something surrounds it

parts.note: tack is slang for food, as in hard tack, ship's biscuit

explanation.surface: A meal is served whose contents are correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a path or route, the line a runner or vehicle follows.

clue.text: Exquisite ordinary French brandy

definitions.meaning: delicate, refined, of the highest quality
in France the word names an everyday brandy

explanation.surface: A connoisseur rates an unremarkable cognac as superb.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for delicate, top-quality work, and the name for basic French brandy.

clue.text: Two ecu the pressman gave up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read bottom to top, so this pair of pieces is reversed

parts.note: taken as written: the ecu was an old European currency unit
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A journalist surrenders a pair of old European coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gave up' turns the whole run ECU + ED backwards; the run is reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A deuce is the two in a pack of cards or on a die.

clue.text: Beer found on the street is no longer fresh

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drink left lying on the pavement has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread or beer that has lost its freshness is stale.

clue.text: Indicate a guilty person by publishing identification by genetic analysis

parts.note: to finger someone is slang for naming them as the culprit
printing is the business of publishing books

explanation.surface: A newspaper names a suspect after the results of DNA tests.
explanation.walkthrough: Genetic profiling from DNA is commonly called 'genetic' followed by this word, by analogy with marks left by fingertips.
explanation.definitionFit: DNA profiling is widely known by this name, matching a person by their genetic pattern.

clue.text: Helped the fool first to begin education

parts.note: an ass is a fool
1st, written with a letter I for the figure one, gives IST

explanation.surface: A dunce was given a leg up at the start of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' becomes IST by writing 1st with the figure one as the letter I; 'to begin' is a loose link, with ED, the short form of education, closing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have assisted someone is to have given them a hand.

clue.text: Crazy sycophants slay shrinks, perhaps

indicators.note: crazy means wild or mad, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Unhinged flatterers kill off psychiatrists.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinks is slang for psychiatrists, and Freudian analysts are one example, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Brilliant person, the socialist, principally acted

parts.note: a star is a brilliant performer
red is a common label for a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: A celebrated left-wing actor took the leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who took the lead role in a film or play is said to have headlined it.

clue.text: Evil sage reported to be genuine

indicators.note: reported speech is spoken, so these words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: sin is evil and a seer is a sage or prophet

explanation.surface: A wicked wise man is said to be honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heartfelt and honest, without pretence, is genuine.

clue.text: A lady who was on the scene right from the beginning

definitions.text: who was on the scene right from the beginning

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal, so a female or lady

explanation.surface: A woman was present from the very start of events.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'A lady' the person present; in fact the definition is the man of Genesis, the first human.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man was created before anyone else, so he was there from the start.

clue.text: Sharp, active police force with resident rector

parts.note: A is a grammatical abbreviation for active

indicators.note: a resident lives inside a place, so this piece is lodged within the other

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A keen detective unit operates with a vicar living among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent, sharp, biting taste or smell is described as acrid.

clue.text: Frequency is painful, we hea5

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken aloud, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: something that is painful hurts

explanation.surface: A recurring ache is said to be agony.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of frequency is the hertz, one cycle per second.

clue.text: Against new tariffs initially

annotationWithheld.why: Against new tariffs initially: the answer is the first letters of all four words, so 'Against' is both definition and a letter source and 'initially' is both indicator and a letter source

clue.text: David Oliver provided something to be worshipped

indicators.note: the two names provide the letters, which sit across the join between them

explanation.surface: A man named David Oliver supplied a cult object.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a statue or image worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Made notes up on the animals

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to have sung is to have made musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone jotted down observations on wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus are wildebeest, large African antelopes.

clue.text: The choirscreen's surprisingly rose red

definitions.note: the possessive 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that these letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A church screen turns out, unexpectedly, to be pinkish-red.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Mild man and I meet at hospital department

parts.note: Len is a man's name
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A man and I meet up in a hospital clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient judge is gentle and forgiving, so the word can mean mild.

clue.text: Swindlers cheated and led astray with rupees

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Con men took people in and led them off course for Indian money.
explanation.definitionFit: A diddler is British slang for a cheat or swindler.

clue.text: Shed waste

definitions.meaning: to shed is to give out, as in shedding money
to waste money is to squander it

explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for paying out money and one for frittering it away.
